C0.note: Approval-based voting rules with variable number of winners; axiomatic and experimental analysis.

C1.quote: We axiomatically analyze established and new shortlisting methods
C1.note: Axiomatic analysis (Sect. 4) is the largest share; simulations (synthetic, Sect. 5.1) and Hugo real-world data (EM). Complexity only noted briefly (Prop. 1).

C2.3.quote: voters have only a noisy perception of these values
C2.3.note: Voters hold perceptions of quality and the paper refers to 'preferences' and to voters' beliefs/biases.

C2.4.quote: We interpret a voter’s approval of a candidate as the
C2.4.note: Approval is interpreted as a preference for inclusion; rules applied directly to ballots with no statement about sincerity or misreporting. Introduction also speaks of voters who 'announce their preferences' by filing approval ballots.

C3.1.quote: We have not considered strategic voting in this paper
C3.1.note: Noise/bias models are not strategic misreporting.

C3.2.note: Voters are modelled as approving with likelihood tied to quality; no statement that submitted equals held attitude in terms of sincerity.

C4.1.note: Input is APPR but the paper does not use voter utility, welfare or satisfaction. Efficiency is argued for in terms of approval scores and Pareto efficiency among shortlists; the 'objective quality' belongs to candidates. A weak case for voter welfare in the Pareto argument, but no utilities.

C5.1.quote: efficient shortlists are Pareto efficient among shortlists of the same size
C5.1.note: Efficiency axiom; also precision against objective quality in experiments.

C5.2.quote: Efficiency can also be argued for from the perspective of voters
C5.2.note: Pareto efficiency evaluated on approval ballots with no statement relating them to held attitudes; precision in simulations is measured against objective quality, but the formal efficiency criterion is on input.

VOT.quote_behav: Our base assumption is that voters approve an alternative with likelihood qc.
VOT.note: Voters' approvals are generated by a fixed stochastic model (noise/bias); no strategic action. Strategic voting explicitly not considered.
